A research bot read three point five hours as thirty-five.
By the time anyone noticed, it was in a Short, two posts, the landing page, its preview image, and a waitlist email.
Taint plus Receipts keeps every claim, the source quote behind it, and everything shipped on top of it, in one FalkorDB graph.
Then we hand it to an agent. Gemini only sees the world through MCP graph tools. It checks receipts, and uses PageRank to see how load-bearing the bad claim is.
One correction, and FalkorDB walks every derived-from path, up to ten hops.
It plans the recall, most-viewed first, and uses shortest path to show exactly why the Short is wrong, right down to the source line.
Then it re-queues the fixes, and writes each owner a recall memo, stored in the graph.
Next session. Reel starts with no memory but the graph. It finds its tasks and the memo, fixes the video and captions, and hands the script to Quill.
Quill picks up Reel's handoff in its own fresh session. Memory and coordination live in the graph, not the chat.
And the rules are enforced in code. Corrections need a receipt, the public MCP endpoint is read-only, and spend is capped.
At twenty-six thousand nodes and ten hops, the cascade takes under a millisecond.
Taint plus Receipts. One wrong number, every place it reached, fixed biggest audience first.
